cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: Consistent hashing assigns keys to servers so that adding or removing a server moves only about 1/M of the keys instead of nearly all. Plain hash(key) mod M remaps almost every key when M changes.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: Servers and keys are hashed onto the same ring; each key goes to the first server clockwise. Virtual nodes place each server on the ring many times so load stays even. Used in Cassandra and DynamoDB partitioning, cache client sharding, load balancers and CDNs.

questions.q: Does consistent hashing alone guarantee even load?
questions.a: No. With one point per server, slices can be very uneven. Virtual nodes fix that.

questions.q: How many keys move with mod-N hashing on resize?
Where is the key placed on the ring?
questions.a: On the first server found walking clockwise from the key's position.
